title: PREDICTIVE
tagline: Real scikit-learn churn model, Optuna-tuned, MLflow-tracked, FastAPI + React, with SHAP explainability, a cost-optimal threshold, and a Docker/Postgres/Redis stack verified from a fresh checkout.
note: Built as a vertical slice of a 10-app enterprise master-prompt, then put through a full remediation pass using 3 real Claude Code subagents (ML_ENGINEER, FULLSTACK_ENGINEER, VERIFICATION_ENGINEER) with scoped file ownership and JSON handoffs, exactly as the original spec required. Requirement audit went from 19 PASS / 25 FAIL to 33 PASS / 13 FAIL out of 57 tracked requirements (REQUIREMENTS_AUDIT.md in the repo has the full row-by-row trail). Deploy-ready (Docker Compose, CI workflow), not deployed to a live host, no cloud account was created or paid for.
problem: Telecom companies lose revenue to customer churn, and want to know: which customers are likely to leave, and why? This project builds a real, evaluated machine-learning answer rather than a dashboard mockup: train and tune a model on the public IBM Telco Customer Churn dataset, calibrate and explain it, optimize its decision threshold against a business cost model, and serve it behind a real API and frontend with authentication, logging, and rate limiting.
built:
An end-to-end ML application with a full remediation pass, not a notebook:

  • Training pipeline (ml/train.py): a stratified 80/20 holdout, 5-fold cross-validation fit only inside the pipeline (no leakage), Optuna-tuned HistGradientBoosting (25 trials, CV-only), three baseline models, isotonic calibration, real SHAP (TreeExplainer/LinearExplainer, exact for whichever model wins, a real bug where the SHAP values were computed in the wrong feature space was found and fixed mid-build), and a business-cost-optimal decision threshold chosen from out-of-fold predictions on the training split only, never the test set.
  • MLflow experiment tracking (local file store) logging every candidate model's params and metrics.
  • FastAPI service with Pydantic validation, API-key authentication on the two write-adjacent endpoints, PostgreSQL prediction logging (degrades cleanly if the DB is unreachable), and a Redis-backed rate limiter, all three verified live against a real Docker Compose stack, not just unit-tested.
  • React/Vite/Tailwind frontend with a canvas intro that does a genuine camera zoom into one selected point before morphing into the real form (an earlier plain-fade version was replaced after review), a prediction studio, an explainability view, a model-comparison table, and a drift monitor explicitly labeled synthetic.
  • 29 pytest tests plus a real Playwright + axe-core browser suite and a Vitest frontend unit suite.

steps.title: Get the real data and define one feature contract
steps.body: Downloaded the public IBM Telco Customer Churn CSV (7,043 customers) and wrote ml/schema.py as the single source of truth for feature names and allowed categories, imported by both the training pipeline and the API's Pydantic model.

steps.title: Train, tune, and track three real models without leaking the test set
steps.body: A stratified 80/20 split is held out before anything else touches the data. Optuna searches HistGradientBoosting's hyperparameters using only cross-validated ROC-AUC on the training split; MLflow logs every candidate run.

steps.title: Fix a real SHAP bug, then optimize the decision threshold against cost
steps.body: An independent review caught that the shipped model's SHAP values had been computed with a permutation-importance fallback zipped against the wrong feature-name array, the published bars were mislabeled. Fixed to always compute exact SHAP (TreeExplainer or LinearExplainer) in the same transformed feature space the names come from, with an assertion guarding the array-length match. Separately, a business-cost threshold (illustrative FN=$500 / FP=$50) is chosen from out-of-fold training predictions only, a dedicated test asserts the selection code never references the test split.

steps.title: Add real auth, logging, and rate limiting, verified against live Docker containers
steps.body: X-API-Key auth, PostgreSQL prediction logging, and Redis-backed rate limiting were each verified against actually-running containers: a request without a key gets a live 401, a logged prediction was queried back out of Postgres, and the 61st request in a window got a real 429. An independent verification pass then found and fixed two real bugs this introduced: a stray CLI line in requirements.txt that broke every fresh Docker build, and a frontend that forgot to send the new auth header entirely, both confirmed fixed by rebuilding from a clean docker compose down -v.

steps.title: Automated browser verification, not just manual screenshots
steps.body: A real Playwright + axe-core suite now runs against the live app (intro → form reveal, a full predict-and-see-result flow, an accessibility scan, mobile/desktop/reduced-motion checks), plus a Vitest unit suite for the frontend client code.

29/29 backend tests passed (model + API, including the negative-input gate and the threshold-never-sees-test-data regression test), 5/5 Playwright tests passed (including a real axe-core accessibility scan with zero serious/critical violations), full Docker Compose stack verified healthy from a fresh checkout with real auth/logging/rate-limiting proof. Requirement audit: 33 PASS / 10 PARTIAL / 13 FAIL / 1 BLOCKED out of 57 tracked requirements, up from 19/12/25/1 before this pass, full row-by-row detail in REQUIREMENTS_AUDIT.md.
